title: Oak-Poached Tri-Tip with Espresso-Lime Gravy
description: Thin slices of lean tri-tip carry a savory oak-smoked gravy with just a trace of espresso and lime.
equipment: Small enamel Dutch oven with tight lid, sized to hold the food snugly

ingredients.name: lean trimmed beef tri-tip
ingredients.note: Intact muscle with fat cap and silver skin removed.

ingredients.name: low-sodium beef broth
ingredients.note: Use plain broth made from meat, bones and water, with no added vegetable blend or seasonings.

ingredients.name: hot drinking water
ingredients.note: Keep ready; use only as needed to maintain liquid depth or make up the sauce measure.

steps.title: Heat the Traeger
steps.text: Preheat the Traeger Silverton 610 to 275°F with oak pellets, about 15 minutes with the lid closed.

steps.title: Warm the braising liquid
steps.text: Bring {broth} with {espresso}, {garlic} and {cumin} just to a simmer in the open Dutch oven on the stove, about 3–6 minutes.

steps.title: Smoke the braising liquid
steps.text: Move the uncovered pot to the Traeger grate. Close the smoker lid and smoke the liquid for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Cut against the grain
steps.text: Follow the grain in {beef} and divide it where the direction changes. Rotate each piece and slice across its grain into 1/3-inch slices.

steps.title: Poach the slices
steps.text: Lay the slices in the smoked liquid without packing them tightly. Top up with {topup} to just cover. Lid immediately with no stall wrap.

steps.title: Check individual slices
steps.text: Cook covered at 275°F for 6–16 minutes, checking the thickest slices sideways from 6 minutes. Transfer each to a covered bowl with hot juices once it reaches 145°F.

steps.title: Rest in the juices
steps.text: Rest the covered beef off heat for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Measure the sauce base
steps.text: Skim excess fat from the braising liquid. Measure 3/4 cup into the HexClad skillet, topping up with {topup} if needed.

steps.title: Season the base
steps.text: Stir {aminos} into the measured broth.

steps.title: Mix the slurry
steps.text: Stir {starch} into {water} until completely smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the skillet liquid to a boil. Whisk in the stirred slurry and simmer for 1 minute, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Finish with lime
steps.text: Stir {lime} into the gravy off heat.

steps.title: Spoon over the slices
steps.text: Divide the beef between shallow bowls and pour the gravy over both, turning the slices once to coat.

notes: Make ahead: Slice the cold beef and refrigerate it covered up to a day ahead. Option A uses espresso and lime. For gentler Option B, omit both and stir a small dab of black garlic puree into the finished gravy. Refrigerate promptly in shallow portions and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze individual portions surrounded by sauce for up to 2 months to protect their moisture. Fridge reheat: Warm one portion covered in its sauce in the HexClad over medium-low heat. Turn gently, adding a splash of water if needed. Check after 6 minutes and continue until the food reaches 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator. Follow the fridge reheating directions and stir the sauce smooth. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 228 kcal, 32.3 g protein, 3.8 g total carbohydrate, 8.0 g fat, 0.1 g fiber, 132 mg sodium. Includes the measured broth and sauce. Sodium varies with your broth.
